construction_rules: Every target is a row in `judgments` held on this machine. A target that is not held is allowed ONLY where the task's expected behaviour is a refusal, and it is marked as such.

Queries are written from the legal question, never by copying the target's language. The leakage guard in the binder measures the longest shared word sequence between query and target text and fails the task above 6 words.
Paraphrases of one question share a `proposition_family` and count as ONE observation when scoring.
`generated` is true only where a query was produced mechanically from a stored field (a citation string, a case number). Everything else is authored.

LONG_FACT_PATTERN and PASTED_PASSAGE tasks are PRODUCT_REQUIRED / CURRENTLY_UNSUPPORTED: the 500-character API cap cannot execute them today. They stay in the set. Removing them to make the benchmark runnable would delete the requirement.

My client is a 29 year old man working in a private firm in Bengaluru. He met the complainant through a colleague in 2021 and they were in a relationship for about three years, during which they travelled together on several occasions, and both families were aware. In 2024 the relationship broke down after his parents refused the match on caste grounds. In 2025 the complainant lodged a first information report alleging that the entire relationship had been on a false promise of marriage and that consent had therefore been vitiated. The investigating officer filed a charge sheet without recording the complainant's parents, who had earlier told the police that they knew of the relationship. My client now seeks to have the proceedings quashed. I need the authorities on when a consensual relationship between adults that later breaks down can be treated as consent obtained under a misconception of fact, and in particular whether the complainant's own conduct, education and social background are relevant to that assessment.

tasks.query: The accused was arrested in March 2021 in a case involving an alleged trespass and assault at his company premises during a celebration. The investigation dragged on for nearly five years without a final report being filed, and no reasons for the delay were ever recorded or intimated to the Magistrate. In the meantime the accused has been required to attend the police station repeatedly and his business has suffered. He now wants a direction that the investigation be concluded within a fixed time, or in the alternative that the proceedings be brought to an end. I need the provisions that impose outer limits on the duration of an investigation under the new criminal procedure code, whether those limits are mandatory or directory, and what a High Court can do when an investigating officer has simply not complied with them.

My clients took premises on what they say was an oral lease running from 2018. They paid a sum described in correspondence as an advance towards the transfer of leasehold rights, and there is a WhatsApp exchange in which the other side calls it an advance. The premises were vacated in June 2022 and possession handed over, but the money was never refunded, and a cheque issued in September 2023 towards repayment was dishonoured. The commercial court decreed recovery. On appeal we say there was never a lease at all, because no instrument was executed and no stamp duty was paid, and that the amount was adjusted against transfer expenses. I need authorities on whether an oral lease can be proved where a local law requires an instrument, and on whether an admitted receipt of money can be retained by simply describing it as an advance.

PASTED FROM AN OPPONENT'S WRITTEN SUBMISSIONS: "It is well settled that where the cognizance of the case has in fact been taken and the case has proceeded to termination, the invalidity of the precedent investigation does not vitiate the result, unless miscarriage of justice has been caused thereby. The learned Special Public Prosecutor submits that if cognizance is in fact taken on a Police Report vitiated by the breach of a mandatory provision relating to investigation, there can be no doubt that the result of the trial which follows it cannot be set aside unless the illegality in the investigation can be shown to have brought about a miscarriage of justice." — which judgment is this passage taken from, and is it still good law?
tasks.notes: deliberate leakage: the passage IS the target's language, because that is what a pasted passage is. Excluded from the leakage guard by design and marked so, since the task is source identification, not concept retrieval.
